title: The grey blocks: which half of your complaint is this?
question: In your screenshot you said 'large uniform gray blocks with blurry light coming off'. Is the block itself — this rectangular silhouette, flat-toned, hard corners — the thing that looks bad, or were you only objecting to the light? If it is the block, is it the shape or the flatness?
context_md:
Your complaint could mean two things and the fixes are unrelated, so I would rather ask than spend the detour on the wrong one.

This is canyon seed 1 at 8x. The formation left-of-centre on the floor is a speleothem. **It is flowstone, not crystal — it emits nothing.** Only ~15% of formations are crystal; the rest are pale cap-rock stone that merely sits inside another crystal's halo, which is likely why they read as though they are glowing.

**What I already know about its shape, so you do not need to tell me:** the widening rule writes at most **2 columns**, with a single secondary column at 3/5 the height. So the silhouette is a rectangle, or a rectangle with one step. There is no taper. Round 5 (running now) raises formation heights substantially — median 3, to a heavy tail reaching 25+ — and a taller rectangle is a worse rectangle, so I expect this to get *more* objectionable before it gets better unless the taper is fixed in the same round.

**What I am unsure of and want your eye on:** whether the flat tone is also part of it. Flowstone uses four palette tones spanning 154-192 luma, which at cave depth compresses to roughly a 10-unit spread — present, but possibly invisible. If you say the flatness bothers you, that is a different fix from the silhouette and I will treat them separately.
